Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 19-Nov-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIRST SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  SUBJECT: ECE 1071/ECE_1071 BASIC ELECTRONICS  
  BASIC ELECTRONICS [ECE 1071]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                        Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  a  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               A silicon diode has reverse saturation current of 1pA at 20o C.                                          (4)  
  Determine:  
  $$i) Diode bias voltage when ID=3mA.$$  
  ii) Diode current when temperature is 100o C.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
1B)               What is the minimum allowable value of VDD if M1 must not enter the triode region if                     (3)  
  $$µ n C ox =200µA/V2$$  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)               With appropriate circuit and waveforms, explain the working of half wave rectifier with capacitive       (3)  
  filter.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
2A)               A Half wave rectifier is given an input of rms 220V, 50 Hz through a transformer with turns ratio        (4)  
  10:1. If the circuit uses an ideal diode, determine (a) DC output voltage (b) Rectifier efficiency (c)  
  DC output voltage if a capacitor of 1mF is connected across 1kΩ load resistance.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2B)               For a Zener network, RS = 500Ω, VZ = 12V and Vi = 50V. Determine the minimum and maximum                 (3)  
  values of RL and load current so that Zener diode remains in ON state and safe, given that ZMax  
  $$I    =$$  
  
  Page #1

2 mA and P ZMin =500mW. Draw the circuit diagram for the same.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2C)   Explain the significance of CMRR in an op-amp. If inputs V1 =60µV and V2 =30µV is given to the            (3)  
  non-inverting and inverting terminals of an OPAMP, respectively. The common mode gain of the  
  OPAMP is 40dB and CMRR is 60dB. Calculate the output voltage.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3A)   Implement the following output function using inverting op-amps. Choose feedback resistance as            (4)  
  $$R f=10kΩ.$$  
  $$Vo= V1 -5V2 - 3V3$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3B)   A 7-bit even parity Hamming code is used to encode a given 4-bit data. The codeword received at           (3)  
  the receiver is "0110101". Decode the codeword to determine the transmitted data, assuming a  
  single error occurred.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3C)   Calculate using 2's complement subtraction:                                                               (3)  
  (i) 68.75(10) - 27.50(10)  
  Convert A23.35(16) into Octal and Decimal equivalent.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
4A)   (i) Using KMAP, simplify the following Boolean expression and obtain the circuit?                         (4)  
  
  
  (ii) A Boolean expression has highest min-term of 35. How many cells are required in KMAP to  
  express this problem? Justify your answer.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4B)   With aid of relevant logical circuit, truth table and timing diagram Illustrate the working of negative   (3)  
  edge triggered 4- bit ripple up counter using JK Flip flop  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4C)   Analyze the operation of a 4-bit Serial-In Serial-Out (SISO) shift register by constructing its logical (3)  
  circuit and truth table for input data sequence of 1100. Explain how data propagates through the flip-  
  flops with each clock pulse.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5A)   An audio signal of 15 sin(2π·1500·t) volts amplitude is used to modulate a carrier of 60                  (4)  
  sin(2π·20000·t) volts. Calculate:  
  i) Modulation index  
  ii) Sideband frequencies  
  $$iii) BandwidthTotal power delivered if R = 2 kΩ$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
5B)   Demonstrate the working of a basic communication system with its block diagram. Explain each              (3)  
  component.  
  
  Page #2

Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
5C)                   Demonstrate the differences between ASK, FSK, and PSK by sketching and interpreting their         (3)  
  waveforms with an example of 4-bit data.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"
